task.text: `Counter` is not thread-safe. Give it an asynchronous front that never needs a lock.

Implement `ActiveCounter(Counter servant)`. Callers get a `CompletableFuture<Integer>` immediately; a single scheduler thread runs every request against the servant. `Counter` is given: do not edit it.

items: `add(int)` resolves to the new total, `total()` to the current one.
Requests run one at a time, in arrival order, only on the scheduler thread. Callers never block.
A request that throws fails its own future; later requests still run.
`close()` finishes accepted requests, stops the scheduler, returns after it exited, and refuses later requests.

checks.title: add and total resolve to the right values
Only the scheduler thread touches the servant
Callers never wait for a busy servant
A failing request fails only its future
close drains accepted work and stops
The servant is a private final field

hints.text: Turn each call into a message. The caller only creates a future and leaves the message in an inbox. Thread safety then comes from who reads the inbox, not from locks around the servant.

Keep a `LinkedBlockingQueue<Runnable>` and start one thread in the constructor that loops on `take()`. Each message runs the servant call and completes the future, or completes it exceptionally. `close()` queues a stop marker and joins.
